quote: I've always despised solar panels, to be totally honest.
stewart_read: This is a cost/skepticism-adjacent objection stated at the very top of the call, before verify even begins. The rep does not acknowledge it at all — he simply continues past it to build rapport with 'You're gonna love these ones,' then the customer keeps talking.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically letting her keep talking to gather more context before responding — but no later moment in the call returns to address the 'despised' comment directly, so the deferral is never redeemed.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly acknowledge strong negative priors ('despised solar panels') even in one line before moving on — a dropped strong statement like this can resurface later as buyer's remorse if unaddressed.

quote: I'm a widow now, and the bills are crazy when you live alone and you only have one income coming in.
stewart_read: This is a textbook vulnerability trust-gift per the schema's own vulnerability_disclosure_handling directive — widowhood plus single-income financial strain, volunteered unprompted in the first minute. The rep's very next line is a scripted transition into verify questions with zero acknowledgment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been trying to move quickly to avoid dwelling on a sad topic — but the schema explicitly treats skip-and-move-on as the failure mode, not a protective choice.
coaching_implication: This is the single biggest miss on the call. Coach: even one sentence — 'I'm sorry to hear that, and I bet that's exactly why the bill is such a pain point' — would have anchored the entire rest of the pitch to her actual motivation.

quote: I've got a few questions, and then we can build your estimate, and then we can get you talking to a specialist to see what we can even do for you. Is that cool?
stewart_read: Rep transitions past both the despised-solar comment and the widow disclosure with a purely procedural line, missing the chance to tie the upcoming questions to her stated pain ('we're going to look at exactly what's driving that bill up since you lost your husband's income').
coaching_implication: Show the rep how a one-line tieback between the customer's own words and the next script step keeps the emotional thread alive instead of resetting to procedure.

quote: come July, August, September, it's close to 800 because of sprinklers and dehumidifiers and air conditioning.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a strong seasonal bill figure ($800) unprompted, well above the $250 baseline she gave seconds earlier. Rep's response is a flat 'Okay. Yeah. Yeah.' with no reflection or flip.
coaching_implication: Coach the ask+acknowledge+flip pattern here directly: '800 in the summer — that's real money leaving your pocket every year, that's exactly what we want to eliminate.'

quote: No. I can't do that. I'm not that educated.
stewart_read: The customer self-initiates the verbal read-back of her bill's usage graph before the rep proactively pivots away from the text-a-photo ask — she reads out the 22.5% increase and daily kWh numbers herself while the rep is largely passive. The rep does not proactively recognize the low-tech friction signal and offer the verbal read-back; the customer does the adapting.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally letting her self-solve to save time — but his later line 'so what phone do you have' shows he was still planning to pursue the photo/text path rather than treating her read-back as sufficient, so the pivot wasn't a deliberate strategic choice.
coaching_implication: Coach faster recognition of the elderly_low_tech_protocol trigger — when a customer says 'I'm not that educated' about a phone task, that is the cue to immediately validate and switch to verbal capture rather than continuing toward the photo/text path anyway.

quote: Yes. I would. But I don't wanna hear that it's gonna cost me $20 for this stuff. I mean, I literally want I mean, at the most, like, $2 out of my pocket.
stewart_read: This directly echoes her earlier widow/single-income disclosure and is a clear cost objection at the point of booking. Rep's response is generic reassurance rather than a flip connecting the program to her stated financial reality.
coaching_implication: This is the second touch of the same underlying concern (see multi_touch_patterns) — coach the rep to name it explicitly: 'given everything you told me about being on one income now, that's exactly why we build these to save you money from day one.'

quote: I don't want anything that I'm gonna have to owe over time. I'm debt free. I don't wanna owe anything.
stewart_read: Third touch of the same financial-anxiety thread; the rep does not respond to this line at all before moving straight into scheduling logistics ('Okay. So can you do tomorrow a call?').
coaching_implication: This unresolved concern must go to the closer explicitly — the customer has stated a hard boundary (debt-free, no financing) three times and it was never addressed on this call.
